response.consequence: On shutdown with a timeout, some flusher processes can be left running and not terminated. They are only cleaned up by daemon-exit handling, so they may keep flushing or producing during or after the consumer's shutdown.
response.explanation: The old join() always called terminate() on the single flusher process after waiting. The new per-process loop does `break` when the shared deadline has passed. Any process that comes after that point never gets terminate() called. Example: with timeout=5 and three flusher processes, the first process's wait uses up the 5 seconds. The second and third are skipped and keep running.
response.title: join() skips terminate() for remaining flusher processes once the deadline expires

response.consequence: The test does not wait for the flusher to process the drift change. The assertion `(msg,) = messages` still depends on a race between the flusher and `step.join()`, so the test can fail intermittently. The added sleep gives no protection.
response.explanation: test_basic starts with monkeypatch.setattr("time.sleep", lambda _: None). That replaces the attribute on the time module for the whole test. The added `time.sleep(0.1)` runs after the drift change and looks up `time.sleep` at call time, so it calls the patched lambda and returns at once. The comment says "Give flusher threads time to process after drift change", but no wait happens. The same patch is why the sleep in `test_flusher_processes_limit` never waits either.
response.title: time.sleep(0.1) in test_basic is a no-op because the test patches time.sleep

response.consequence: A hung flusher is not killed on restart. Two flushers then run on the same shards, each with its own Kafka producer, and can produce duplicate segments. Each hang leaks a process, and `join` can leave child processes running on shutdown.
response.explanation: The processes are created with `multiprocessing.get_context("spawn").Process`, which is `SpawnProcess`. `SpawnProcess` derives from `BaseProcess`, not from `multiprocessing.Process` (that is `context.Process`, a sibling class). So `isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process)` is False for every real process. The old code called `self.process.kill()` unconditionally. In `_ensure_processes_alive` the kill is therefore skipped. When the cause is "hang", the stuck process stays alive and a new one is started for the same shards. The same check in `join` (line 346) means `terminate()` is never called either.
response.title: Hung flusher process is never killed: isinstance check against multiprocessing.Process fails for SpawnProcess
